svg.font-family: Calibri, Carlito, 'Noto Sans', 'Segoe UI', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: How a deck's design language and each page's layout are chosen
svg.desc: Stage I settles one design language for the deck: the uploaded template's own, or three authored by a model, gated in code and shown as specimens for the person to choose. Stage II places each page: its material is bound to every archetype by an exact assignment, infeasible bindings are refused, the cheapest feasible one wins, and a page nothing can carry is split.
svg.text: Stage I · one design language per deck
a typed value: canvas, type floor, page vocabulary
Pack: grid, type ramp, colour roles and page archetypes,
slot capacities measured by setting copy in the real face;
every frame seated on one ground
Stage II · one layout per page
kind, items, characters per item, each exhibit's natural aspect
slot left empty, an item left out,
an exhibit below its legible floor
the cheapest wins, ties to the
split the page and bind again
the fallback chain, ending in a plain page
short material cut to its size and set at the optical centre; a monotone patch loop
geometry from the real render; a vision verdict on each changed page
A page is kept only if
its score falls, so a bounded
loop never ends on its worst try;
No model ever emits a coordinate: models choose words, kinds and exhibits; code chooses every position.
